name: constellations

description.en: All 88 constellations recognised by the International Astronomical Union, in 88 cards studied both ways. Front: the constellation's official Latin name; back: its English and Swedish names, with the IAU abbreviation in a note. Names from the IAU's constellation table and Wikidata, checked against NASA, Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin.
description.sv: Alla 88 stjärnbilder som Internationella astronomiska unionen (IAU) erkänner, på 88 kort som övas åt båda hållen. Framsida: stjärnbildens officiella latinska namn; baksida: dess engelska och svenska namn, med IAU:s förkortning i en anteckning. Namnen kommer från IAU:s tabell över stjärnbilderna och från Wikidata och är kontrollerade mot NASA, Wikipedia och Nationalencyklopedin.

method: Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund’s direction, with independent AI reviewers (three review rounds: factual accuracy, language and translation, licensing and documentation; then a final re-check) and machine checks against Wikidata at every build. No human subject expert has reviewed the cards yet.

The list of constellations, their Latin names, abbreviations and English names come from the IAU's page “The Constellations”. Its old address (https://www.iau.org/public/themes/constellations/) returns 404 since the IAU's site was redesigned, and the new iau.org has no constellation page linked from its home page. The page was found in the IAU's own web archive at https://iauarchive.eso.org/public/themes/constellations/ (the reference used by the English Wikipedia article) and downloaded with curl on 2026-10-04; an Internet Archive copy of the old iau.org page from 2023-12-30 was also downloaded and has the identical table. The table under “Charts and tables” was parsed with a short Python script (parse_iau.py, reproduced verbatim under Queries; HTML tags stripped, the download links dropped, the remaining cells read in groups of six: name, pronunciation, abbreviation, English name, genitive, genitive pronunciation). It gives exactly 88 rows.

Each card's front is the IAU name exactly as the table spells it (e.g. “Boötes” with its diaeresis), tagged as Latin. All 88 are tagged Latin by convention, Dorado included: the IAU names serve as the constellations’ scientific Latin names and are declined as Latin (the IAU table gives the genitive “Doradus”), although “dorado” itself is a Spanish word, as the Dorado card’s note says. The back's English text is the table's “English Name” (described on the page as “the popular name in English”) without its leading “the” (“the Great Bear” → “Great Bear”), with three kinds of exception: (a) Coma Berenices: the table reads “the Bernice's Hair”; the deck spells it “Berenice’s Hair”, as the Latin name itself (Berenices) and Wikipedia's Meaning column (“Berenice's hair”) do. (b) Pyxis: the table reads “the Mariner Compass”; the deck uses the usual English form “Mariner’s Compass” (Wikipedia's Meaning column: “mariner's compass”). (c) Eight constellations named after a figure — Andromeda, Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Eridanus, Hercules, Orion, Pegasus and Perseus — have the figure's own name as their English name, which is what English uses for them; the IAU table gives descriptions for seven of them (“the Chained Maiden”, “the Seated Queen”, “the King”, “the River”, “the Hunter”, “the Winged Horse”, “the Hero”; for Hercules it reads “the Hercules”), and those descriptions are quoted in the card's note instead. Using them as answers would have made the reversed cards ambiguous (“Hero” fits Hercules as well as Perseus) and would not translate the Swedish name on the same card (Cassiopeja, Orion, …).

The Swedish names are the Swedish labels (rdfs:label @sv) of the Wikidata items. The items were found with one SPARQL query on https://query.wikidata.org/sparql (listed under Queries) that matches each IAU name against English labels of items that are instances of constellation (Q8928) or a subclass of it and have a short name (P1813); it returned exactly one item for each of the 88 names, and for every item the short name equals the IAU abbreviation. The English and Swedish aliases of the 88 items were fetched with a second query, so that a Wikidata check could also be added where an alias is exactly the card's English text. A first exploratory query (instances of Q8928 only) returned 97 items: it missed Aries and Cancer, which Wikidata types only as zodiac constellation (Q4193029), and included historical or non-IAU constellations (e.g. Sciurus Volans, Marmor Sculptile, Pomum Imperiale); it was used only to see how the data is modelled.

Swedish cross-check: every Swedish label was compared with the table “Tabell över stjärnbilderna” in the Swedish Wikipedia article “Stjärnbild” (wikitext fetched with https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Stj%C3%A4rnbild&prop=wikitext|revid&format=json&formatversion=2, revision 59706601), parsed with a Python script. That script was not kept; the parsing rules are reproduced by parse_svwiki.py (under Queries), written during review round 2, which gives exactly the same 87 rows from the same saved wikitext (the rowspan rows of Giraffen/Camelopardalis are skipped and that row added by hand, as in the original). All 88 Swedish names and all 88 abbreviations agree. The names follow Swedish convention: definite form of a common noun with a lower-case second word (“Stora björnen”, “Södra korset”), and the Swedish forms of personal names (“Cassiopeja”, “Herkules”).

English cross-check: every English name and abbreviation was compared with the “List” table of the English Wikipedia article “IAU designated constellations” (parsed with parse_enwiki.py, under Queries; wikitext fetched with https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=IAU_designated_constellations&prop=wikitext|revid&format=json&formatversion=2, revision 1375575250). The Meaning column agrees with the IAU's English name for most constellations; where it differs (listed in quality control, round 0) the deck keeps the IAU's name, since the IAU is the authority for the list and the Wikipedia column gives a literal meaning rather than a popular name.

Abbreviation and list cross-check: the NASA/GSFC page “Three-Letter Constellation Abbreviations” was downloaded with curl and its table parsed; it lists the same 88 constellations with the same abbreviations (in capitals). NASA and Wikidata spell Boötes without the diaeresis in some places (NASA “Bootes”, Wikidata's Latin label “Bootes”); the deck follows the IAU spelling, which is also Wikidata's English label.

The generator script make_dossier.py (reproduced verbatim under Queries, together with wd_fetch.py and wd_aliases.py, which ran the two Wikidata queries; the raw downloads were kept in a temporary working directory of the authoring agent that is not published) asserts for every card that the IAU abbreviation equals the Wikidata short name, the Swedish Wikipedia abbreviation and the NASA abbreviation, and that the Wikidata Swedish label equals the Swedish Wikipedia name; it then writes each card with its evidence from all five sources. Each card’s note gives the IAU abbreviation and, in the authoring agent’s own words, an explanation where the English and Swedish names clearly differ in meaning (Boötes, Capricornus, Cetus, Corvus, Hydra, Hydrus, Horologium, Pictor, Reticulum, Taurus, Telescopium), where the IAU’s popular name is not used as the answer, or where the name itself needs a word (Dorado); notes on Swedish variants (Cassiopeia, Eridanus, Vela) were added in review round 1. Smaller nuances (e.g. Vela “Sails” / Seglet, singular) get no note.

Review rounds 1–3 were applied to the dossier by apply_rounds.py and round 4 by apply_round4.py (both reproduced verbatim under Queries). apply_rounds.py reads the saved downloads and review fetches (NE openings, English Wikipedia leads) and edits the dossier that make_dossier.py wrote; replay.py (also under Queries) re-ran it on a saved copy of that pre-review dossier and found the result identical to the published dossier before round 4.

Swedish names, independent check (added in review rounds 1–2): for every card, Nationalencyklopedin’s article was fetched by the script ne_fetch.py (under Queries) from https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<Swedish name, lower case, spaces as hyphens>, falling back to <…>-(stjärnbild), and the opening sentence (the free part of the article) kept as evidence. NE gives the card’s Swedish name as the headword for 85 of the 88 cards. The three others: Cassiopeja (NE’s headword is “Cassiopeia”, with “Cassiopeja” as a variant), Eridanus (NE’s main article is “Floden Eridanus”; “Eridanus” is a cross-reference to it) and Seglet (NE calls it “Seglen”, plural). These cards keep the Wikidata and Swedish Wikipedia name, which the builder checks, and give NE’s form in the note.

English names, second check (added in review round 3): where English Wikipedia’s list renders the IAU’s English name differently, and for the meanings given in the notes, the lead sections of the English Wikipedia articles on those constellations were fetched with the MediaWiki API (under Queries) and the sentence that confirms the name or meaning is quoted in the card’s evidence. The Swedish names of species used in the notes (korp, stenbock, guldmakrill) were looked up as Wikidata labels and are checked at every build.

Every card has machine checks against Wikidata, run by the builder: the English label equals the IAU Latin name, the Swedish label equals the card's Swedish name, and the short name (P1813) equals the IAU abbreviation; where Wikidata has the card's English text as an English alias, that alias is checked too.

Study direction is bidirectional: the builder confirms that every English and every Swedish back text is unique in the deck, so the reversed cards (English or Swedish name → Latin name) each have one answer. For 11 constellations the English name is the Latin name (Andromeda, Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Eridanus, Hercules, Lynx, Orion, Pegasus, Perseus, Phoenix, Sculptor), and for six of them the Swedish name is too (Andromeda, Cepheus, Eridanus, Orion, Pegasus, Perseus), so the reversed card gives its answer away; that is inherent to the subject and was accepted.
selection: The deck has exactly the 88 constellations in the IAU's table, which are the constellations the IAU recognises (the list agreed in 1922, with boundaries adopted in 1928 and published in 1930); nothing was added and nothing left out. Historical constellations that the IAU does not recognise (Wikidata types some of them as constellations, e.g. Sciurus Volans and Marmor Sculptile) are excluded. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper/Karlavagnen are not constellations and are excluded. Genitive forms, pronunciations, boundaries and star names are left out to keep each card to one fact: the constellation's names.

import json, re
D = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'
w = json.load(open(D + 'enwiki-iau-designated.json'))['parse']['wikitext']
i = w.find('=== List ===')
t = w[i:]
t = t[:t.find('\n|}')]
rows = t.split('\n|-')[2:]


def clean(c):
    c = re.sub(r'<ref[^>]*/>', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'(?s)<ref.*?</ref>', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\{\{efn[^}]*\}\}', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\{\{IPAc-en[^}]*\}\}', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\{\{br\}\}', ' ', c)
    c = re.sub(r'data-sort-value="[^"]*"\s*\|', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]+)\]\]', r'\1', c)
    c = c.replace("''", '')
    return c.strip()


out = {}
for r in rows:
    r = r.strip().lstrip('|').strip()
    first = r.split('\n')[0]
    cells = [clean(c) for c in first.split('||')]
    name = cells[0].strip()
    meaning = cells[8] if len(cells) > 8 else '?'
    out[name] = {'iau': cells[1], 'meaning': meaning}
json.dump(out, open(D + 'enwiki-table.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
iau = json.load(open(D + 'iauarchive-table.json'))
print(len(out))
for r in iau:
    m = out.get(r['name']) or out.get(r['name'].replace('ö', 'o'))
    print(r['name'], '|', r['abbr'], '|', r['english'], '||', m)

For the second warning, Nationalencyklopedin was added as a verification source on every card (85 headwords identical, three variants given in notes); in-the-sky.org’s translation table (https://in-the-sky.org/data/constellations_translations.php, downloaded 2026-10-04) was also looked at but not used, because its Swedish column has evident errors (Circinus “Ormen”, Scutum “Sobieskis sköld”).
